porosity.derivation: 1 - 675 / 1500: the density over the cell wall's own (about 1500 kg/m3, Siau 1995, Wood: Influence of Moisture on Physical Properties)

wettingDepth.note: A first depth of the cells whose water or finish darkens the face.

grain.source: Substances/oak.json: anatomy.endgrain (2 to 4 rows of large earlywood pores)
grain.note: Oak's earlywood vessels are 0.2 to 0.3 mm across (Hoadley 2000, Understanding Wood).

bed.note: A slow-grown French sessile oak lays 1 to 3 mm a year; the middle is taken until boards are measured.

bedAspect.note: How much longer the figure runs along the grain than across it.

hurst.note: As the stones; no measurement of a wood face was read.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range within one board; the measured rows are package means.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range across a finished face.

latewoodFraction.note: The middle of the range; narrow rings of slow-grown oak hold less latewood.

latewoodTone.note: The dense latewood reads darker than the open earlywood; to be measured on a board.

rayFleck.note: The share of a quarter-sawn face the broad rays show on.

rayTone.note: The flecks read paler and glossier than the wood around them.

rayLength.note: Oak's broad rays stand up to several centimetres tall; a first fleck length.

rayWidth.note: A first fleck width across the grain.
